units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 764:13">Yalk. Num. 764</cite> <he>כשתראה שנִתְקְלוּ בדבר וכ׳</he> when thou seest that they (Israel) have stumbled in anything, leap thou against (attack) them.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 3:1">B. Kam. III, 1</cite> <he>המניח … ונ׳ בה ושברה</he> if one left his pitcher on public ground, and another man came and struck against it, and broke it.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 3:4">Ib. 4</cite> <he>ונ׳ הראשון ונפל ונ׳ וכ׳</he> and the first man stumbled and fell, and the second man stumbled over the first.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 28b:13">Ib. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳ באבן ונשוף וכ׳</he> if he struck against a stone, and the vessel was smashed by the stone; <he>נ׳ בקרקע וכ׳</he> if he struck against soft ground, and the vessel was smashed through falling on the stone. Ib. 29ᵇ <he>נ׳ פושע הוא</he> he that does damage by stumbling is legally considered like one criminally negligent; a. fr.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 44:1">Pesik. R. s. 44</cite> <he>הושע</he> … <he>אלא מַתְקֶלֶת</he> Hosea declared her (Israel) nothing more than a stumbler (ref. to <he>כשלת</he>, <cite ref="Hosea 14:2">Hos. XIV, 2</cite>).
